[VARC] Share component record decoding

Route the draw, closure, depend, and subset paths through a single
component record decoder instead of open-coding the walk in each.

Glyph records are immutable for the life of the face, so also cache
the fetched record bytes in the draw scratch; the recursive
component walk then skips repeated CFF2Index offset decoding for
records it has already seen.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

[subset] Address VARC review findings

Assorted follow-ups from the VARC subsetting review: narrower
include guards, pass axis indices through the record decoder, and
simplify closure/depend bookkeeping.

The record-byte fetch in the composite draw walk still ran a count
pre-check around the scratch cache even though the bounds-checked
CFF2Index fetch below it already covers out-of-range coverage
positions; drop the duplicate checks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: The defect is split across two commits and is unreachable from either one alone. Commit bc0a690 ('[VARC] Share component record decoding') introduces a per-face scratch cache (hb_varc_scratch_t::recordBytes) in the VARC composite draw walk: the cache vector is sized to glyphRecords.count, and every raw arrayZ access is guarded by an explicit 'idx < record_count' check, falling back to the bounds-checked CFF2Index fetch otherwise. On its own this commit is correct maintenance and memory-safe on any input. Commit 3236412 ('[subset] Address VARC review findings') removes that guard from the cache read and store, on the stated reasoning that the bounds-checked CFF2Index fetch below it already covers out-of-range coverage positions. That reasoning is subtly wrong: the raw read recordBytes.arrayZ[idx] executes BEFORE the fallback fetch, so when a VARC table's coverage maps a glyph to a coverage index >= glyphRecords.count (a table shape the sanitizer accepts on this batch), the cache read walks past the end of the resize(record_count)-sized heap allocation. Composition: bc0a690 alone keeps the guard, so no out-of-bounds access; 3236412 alone is vacuous, because without bc0a690 there is no recordBytes cache or guard in the dispatcher for its hunk to simplify (the tree is then identical to the pristine batch). Only both edits together produce the reachable heap-buffer-overflow read in VARC::get_path_at, entered via the public API hb_font_draw_glyph / hb_font_get_glyph_extents. A correct fix is therefore non-local: patching only 3236412's diff (restoring the guard) fixes the tip, but recognizing that requires knowing bc0a690 introduced the raw arrayZ access; and 'fixing' only bc0a690's diff (e.g. keeping its guarded form) cannot be expressed without undoing 3236412's apparently benign simplification. Fixing any single commit's diff alone leaves the bug reachable once the other commit's content is present.
